# Turboslide round four, hotfix 4

Kevin's reports on production (https://turboslide.vercel.app, 2026-09-14, afternoon): "resizing isn't working" with a screenshot of a Mark block whose box reads 536 by 343 while the GT glyph stays small in the top left corner; "and pressing space isn't working. make sure to actually test our slide features and make sure they work" with a screenshot of a title reading "NewSlideTemplateemplatelideletee" beside the same stale 536 by 343 readout and a "Click to add text" body placeholder.

Files this hotfix touches are listed at the end of each section.

## 1. The editor walk

By the walker, 2026-09-14, against https://turboslide.vercel.app with headless Chromium (`playwright-core` 1.62.1 from the repo's `node_modules`, Node 24.13.0, viewport 1440 by 900 at device scale 1), under `.turboslide/e2e.lock`, through the product's own UI and its window API (`window.turboslide.studio`).

### 1.1 Why a walk

The round's unit tests and the earlier probes passed while the product failed under Kevin's hands. The probes typed one acknowledged character at a time and never held a handle across a real drag with the events a browser sends (pointerdown, the pointermove stream, pointerup, the click after the drag, focus moving to the handle button). `scripts/probes/editor-walk-probe.mjs <base>` therefore uses the product like a person at human speed: the mouse moves in steps with a pause between them, keys land 40 to 90 ms apart, double clicks are the browser's own, drags hold a handle from pointerdown to pointerup with Shift or Alt held on the keyboard, and Escape is pressed like anyone would. It asserts after every step and writes a table (step, expected, observed, ok) to stdout and to a JSON file (`--json <path>`); every observed value is read from the DOM and from `describe().state`, `slide.get` and `slide.list`, so the table proves what happened. The scratch deck is trashed through File > Move to trash and Delete forever in a `finally` block, then probed for a 404, even after a failure. A step the walk cannot drive is recorded as not driven, never as ok. Exit 1 when a step fails.

Run: `until mkdir .turboslide/e2e.lock; do sleep 5; done; node scripts/probes/editor-walk-probe.mjs --base https://turboslide.vercel.app --json <path>; rmdir .turboslide/e2e.lock`.

### 1.2 What the walk does

One deck from `/new`. The title is typed with spaces and punctuation and committed with Escape (the first write creates the deck and moves the address to `/edit/<id>`). The text battery on the title: a single click mid text and typing, a double click on a word and typing over it, Home, End, a space at the end of the text followed by a 700 ms pause and a word, ArrowLeft and Shift ArrowLeft, typing over a selection, Backspace, Delete, Cmd A with Cmd B and Cmd I, Enter, Cmd Z and Cmd Shift Z inside the text, Shift Enter. The body placeholder: a double click and a sentence, Enter and a second line, Shift Enter and a third, Home, End, the arrows and Backspace, Escape. New slide from the toolbar, Apply layout from the toolbar to the Title layout, a short title and a body typed into it, a shape placed on it (the conversion of a slide with a short title), a long title typed into the converted heading; New slide from the Slide menu; back to the title slide by its filmstrip card. The reported gesture: a mark inserted, selected, resized by its bottom right handle by 330 by 210 px, the readout read during and after the release, the glyph measured against its box, Space with the handle focused, a click on the title and " New Slide Template" typed with spaces, End and Home on the converted title. One of every kind the Insert menu offers, by clicking the menu: a text box (a click on the sheet, then the word "Text" typed into it so it is not an empty placeholder), a rectangle, an arrow, a callout and an equation shape from the four shape categories, a line drawn by a drag, a picture (Image by URL refuses a data URL by its `https?://` rule, so the same `asset.add` and `block.insert` the dialog dispatches were sent through the window API), an icon, a material, a table from the hover grid, a chart, a diagram from the panel; the mark and the code panel with its marks through the window API, because this build has no toolbar Insert card and no palette button and the menubar's Insert menu has no row for them; the logo plates need an asset and stay not driven. Every object is placed in its own cell (`block.set /pos`, the setup for the drags). For every object: a drag by 120 by 80 sheet px from its frame edge, a resize by every one of the eight handles plain, with Shift and with Alt at zoom 100 and by the bottom right handle at zoom 200, each recording the box before and after against the expected box, the content size against the box, the readout during and after the release, the chip, the guides and the revision, with the toolbar's Undo after every drag that changed the box (so no object drifts across the matrix) and one row per kind counting the releases after which the readout stayed. Then: the rectangle rotated by its ring and undone, Shift click, Cmd G, Cmd Option G and Arrange > Group, the group resized, Cmd Option Shift G or Arrange > Ungroup, Cmd D, Delete, Cmd Z, Cmd Shift Z; the second filmstrip card dragged above the first; the layout picker opened from the toolbar and Escape; the theme panel, dark, light and closed; the Slideshow with ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, 3 and Enter, Escape; the Share dialog; every menu (File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, Slide, Arrange, Tools, Extensions, Help) opened and closed with Escape with the console watched; `export.run` PPTX flatten and native through the window API, the browser's download taken and its first bytes checked for the zip magic; and in a `finally` block File > Move to trash, Delete forever on `/decks/trash`, and a GET of `/edit/<id>` that must answer 404.

### 1.4 Root causes

The cited files equal `6679c54` (`git diff --stat HEAD` over `packages/viewer/src/{Editor,InlineText,Gestures,Selection}.tsx`, `packages/chrome/src/{Overlay,EditorShell}.tsx`, `packages/render/src/blocks/{misc,context}.ts`, `packages/render/src/block-css.ts` is empty), so the line numbers are the shipped ones.

W1. The size readout stays after the pointer is released (severity 3; Kevin's stale "536 × 343", the walk's stale "637 × 398" over the Title selection). `packages/viewer/src/Editor.tsx:1878-1896`, the `up` handler of `beginGesture`: line 1885 calls `endGestureState()`, which clears the readout (`setReadout(null)`, `:1776`), and line 1892 then calls `gestureAt(g, now, mods)` to compute the mutations of the release; `gestureAt` (`:1744-1767`) is not pure: for a free resize or rotation it calls `setReadout({ kind: 'size', ... })` at `:1760` (and `:1758` for the angle) as a side effect of computing the preview. The release therefore sets the readout again after clearing it, and nothing clears it afterwards: the readout state lives on the Editor, so it follows the selection ring to whatever is selected next (the Title in Kevin's screenshot). The conversion branch of the release does the same at `:1921`. The rotation readout of the keyboard path has a timer (`showAngle`, `:2605-2609`, `ROTATE_READOUT_MS`); the pointer path has none. The fix is to compute the release mutations without the side effect (a pure `gestureAt`, or `endGestureState()` after the final `gestureAt`), and the walk's step "after the pointer is released the readout clears" guards it.

W2. The mark glyph does not scale with its box (severity 2; Kevin's small GT in a 536 by 343 box). `packages/render/src/blocks/misc.ts:31-38` (`renderMark`) passes `block.w, block.h` to `markSvg`, and `packages/render/src/blocks/context.ts:164` writes them as the svg's `width` and `height` attributes; `packages/render/src/block-css.ts:211` gives `.free > svg[data-type="mark"]` only `display: block; fill: currentColor`, while `:218-219` give the icon and diagram objects `width: 100%; height: 100%` (hotfix 3 causes R4 and R5). The box resizes and the glyph keeps its attribute size (the walk: box 449 by 281 CSS px against a glyph of 113 by 71, attributes 160 by 100). The same fixed sizes are written for the panel's marks (`packages/render/src/blocks/panel.ts:17`, `width="25" height="16"` and `width="50" height="32"`) and the figure mark (`figures.ts:344`, no size, sized by the theme CSS). Fix: a positioned mark writes no size (as `renderIcon` does for a positioned icon, `primitives.ts:603-618`) and `block-css.ts` gives `.free > svg[data-type="mark"]` `width: 100%; height: 100%`; the panel's marks scale with the panel's font size or the box.

W3. A space typed at the end of the text is lost when the next key comes more than 100 ms later (severity 3; Kevin's "pressing space isn't working" and "NewSlideTemplate"). The walk's row: right after the space the run ends in `x` U+00A0 (the browser writes a no-break space for a trailing space in a contenteditable); after a 700 ms pause it ends in `x` with no space at all; the stored text ends in `x`; the word typed next lands as `xy`. In a second, natural instance the body of the new slide typed at 40 to 90 ms per key landed as "Bodycopy, with a comma." `packages/viewer/src/InlineText.tsx:68` sets `TEXT_BURST_MS = 100`; `flushBurst` (`:1104-1117`) reads `text = readText()` through `textFromNode`, which trims a one line pointer (`:234`) and every paragraph of a multiline one (`:236`), and compares it with `raw`, the untrimmed serialization (`:1108-1109`); a trailing space makes `raw !== text`, so `:1110` calls `rewriteEditable(text)`, which replaces the editable's HTML with the trimmed canonical text (`:1095-1102`) and restores the caret from the offsets it recorded. The space the person just typed is gone 100 ms after the keystroke, before the next letter arrives, whenever the pause between two words is longer than 100 ms, which is the pace of a person. The rewrite rule (SPEC-2 0.54) means to normalise split runs and nested wrappers, not to trim; the fix is to compare `raw` with the untrimmed canonical form (trim only in the write, never in the rewrite), or to skip the rewrite while the difference is trailing white space. The caret restore after a rewrite of a shorter text is the likely origin of the duplicated fragments in Kevin's title ("emplate", "lide"): the recorded offset lies past the new text's end and the caret lands elsewhere; the walk did not reproduce the fragments.

W4. Enter in the title slide's body placeholder ends the session and the words typed next are lost (severity 2). `packages/viewer/src/Editor.tsx:1399-1400` (`startEdit`): `const block = blockById(slideNow, run.blockId); const multiline = block !== undefined && isMultilinePath(block, ...)`. `blockById` (`packages/viewer/src/Selection.tsx:146-148`) finds top level slot blocks only; the title slide's `lead` (and `heading`) are pseudo blocks that are slide fields (`Selection.tsx:150-158`, `blockTypeOf`), so `block` is undefined and `multiline` is false. `InlineText.tsx:1276-1291`: Enter on a run that is not multiline calls `finish('enter')`, and the session ends; the letters typed next reach no editor (the stage has no type to edit path, the shell's letter keys are off on the editor), so "Second line" was lost and Shift Enter reopened the run at its end. Google keeps typing on a new line in the subtitle placeholder. Fix: resolve the pseudo block's type through `blockTypeOf` (a `paragraph` is multiline for `/text`) when `blockById` finds nothing.

W5. The layout picker opened with the pointer does not close on Escape (severity 1, suspected). `packages/chrome/src/EditorShell.tsx:2108-2135`: the plate is a `role="dialog"` whose Escape handler is its own `onKeyDown`, so it answers only while focus is inside it; opened by a click on `toolbar.layout` the focus stays on the toolbar button. The local dry run saw the plate open (22 tiles) and stay after Escape; in the production run the click did not open the plate at all (row 748), because the Find and replace dialog the walk's Cmd G probe had opened (Cmd G is Find next, `menus/keys.ts:495`) took the click, so the production row is the walk's, not the product's. An outside press closes the plate (`:2099-2106`). To be rerun with the dialog closed.

W6. Grouping by the keyboard is unverified (severity 2 if real). With a rectangle and a text box selected by a click and a Shift click (the chip reads "2 objects"), the walk pressed Cmd G first, which Google and this build bind to Find next (`menus/keys.ts:495`); the Find and replace dialog opened and its input held the focus when Cmd Option G (the Group binding, `menus/model.ts:1996-1997`) arrived (row 741), and the Arrange menu could not open under the dialog (row 742). The chord matcher runs a menu item only when `isEnabled(item, s.menuContext)` holds and a disabled row swallows the chord (`useEditorKeys.ts:168-216`, `:203-206`); `arrange.group` needs `canGroup`, `model.ts:2908-2909`: `selection.blocks >= 2 && objects`, so whether the shell's menu context counts a Shift click selection is the question the rerun answers (the walk now closes the dialog after the Cmd G probe and reselects the pair, and reads `aria-disabled` on the Arrange > Group row). A second hazard for a person on a Mac: `menus/keys.ts:349-352` compares `event.key.toUpperCase()` with the chord's letter, and Chromium on macOS reports the Option layer character for Option letter chords (Option G is "©"), so Cmd Option G, Cmd Option M (Comment) and Cmd Option Shift H (Version history) may never match from a real keyboard; the walk's synthetic key carries the plain letter and cannot settle this.

W7. A picture object's frame runs 12 sheet px past its box (severity 1). ## 2. The fixes

By the fixer, 2026-09-14, against the walk's findings of section 1. Each fix is at the root cause and carries a unit test or a walk step. The dev server for the walk and the resize spec was `TURBOSLIDE_STORE=tmp TURBOSLIDE_REALTIME=memory TURBOSLIDE_LOCAL_OPEN=1 node_modules/.bin/vite dev --port 4350` from `apps/studio`, under `.turboslide/e2e.lock`, stopped after.

### 2.1 W1: the size and angle readout stayed after the pointer was released

Diagnosis, confirmed against the shipped code. `Editor.tsx`'s pointer up handler cleared the readout with `endGestureState()` and then called `gestureAt` again to compute the release, and `gestureAt` set the readout as a side effect of computing the preview, so the release set the readout after clearing it and nothing cleared it afterwards. The readout state lives on the Editor, so it then followed the selection ring to whatever was selected next.

Fix. The readout now lives in one gesture state machine, `packages/viewer/src/gesture-life.ts`: a `down` starts a gesture with no readout, a `move` shows the readout that move computed, and every end event returns to the idle state with no readout. The end events are the pointer's release, the browser's cancel, the element losing its pointer capture, the window losing focus during the drag, and Escape. `gestureAt` is now pure: it returns the readout it would show rather than setting it, and the pointer move sets the readout through the state machine while the release computes its mutations with the same function and shows nothing. `beginGesture` binds the four extra end listeners for the length of the drag and removes them when it ends. A selection change while no gesture is down clears the state machine, so a click elsewhere never inherits a previous gesture's readout. Escape during a drag cancels the drag: the object returns to its committed box and nothing is written. The stage's own Escape handler yields while a gesture is down, so the gesture's own listener cancels it.

Tests. `packages/viewer/src/__tests__/gesture-life.test.ts` pins the reducer: the readout shows only between the press and the end, every one of the five end events returns to idle, a move or a selection change after the end never revives a readout, and a new press starts clean. The walk proves it end to end: "after the pointer is released the readout clears", "the readout is gone while the title is being edited", "the angle readout clears after the ring is released", "Escape during a drag cancels it", "the window losing focus during a drag ends it", and the per kind "readout cleared" rows.

Files: `packages/viewer/src/gesture-life.ts` (new), `packages/viewer/src/Editor.tsx`, `packages/viewer/src/__tests__/gesture-life.test.ts` (new).

### 2.2 W2: the mark glyph did not scale with its box

Diagnosis, confirmed. `renderMark` passed the block's width and height to `markSvg`, which wrote them as the svg's `width` and `height` attributes, and `block-css.ts` gave a positioned mark only `display` and `fill`, so the box resized and the glyph kept its attribute size.

Fix, the rule hotfix 3 used for the icon and the diagram (SPEC-5-amendments A4). `markSvg` takes a `sized` flag; `renderMark` passes it false for a mark object of the canvas (a block with `pos`), so a positioned mark writes no size and the symbol keeps its own ratio inside the box. `block-css.ts` gives `.free > svg[data-type="mark"]` (and the linked form) `width: 100%; height: 100%`. A flow mark keeps its pixel size byte for byte.

Tests. `packages/render/src/__tests__/blocks.test.ts` asserts a flow mark writes `width` and `height` and a mark object writes neither and carries the fill rule; `scripts/canvas-fidelity.mjs` stays green (the blank template's converted title mark renders at its measured box). The walk: "the mark glyph scales with its box" and the 25 mark resize rows.

Files: `packages/render/src/blocks/misc.ts`, `packages/render/src/blocks/context.ts`, `packages/render/src/block-css.ts`, `packages/render/src/__tests__/blocks.test.ts`.

### 2.3 W3: a space at the end of the text was lost after a pause

Diagnosis, confirmed. `flushBurst` rewrote the editable from the trimmed write form whenever the untrimmed serialization differed from it, so a trailing space made the two differ and the rewrite replaced the editable's HTML with the trimmed text one burst after the keystroke, before the next letter arrived.

Fix. The rewrite rule (SPEC-2 0.54) is meant to normalise a run the browser split or a wrapper it nested, not to trim. `burstRewrite(raw)` now compares what the DOM serializes to with its own canonical form (`canonicalText`), which keeps the white space at the ends of every paragraph, and rewrites only when they differ. The trimming stays where it belongs, in the write (`textFromNode`). The burst window is unchanged.

Tests. `packages/viewer/src/__tests__/inline-text.test.ts` (`burstRewrite`): a trailing space is not a rewrite, the white space at either end of any paragraph is left alone, and a string that is not its own canonical form is rewritten from the canonical form with its ends kept. The walk: "a space typed at the end of the text, then a pause, then a word".

Files: `packages/viewer/src/InlineText.tsx`, `packages/viewer/src/__tests__/inline-text.test.ts`.

### 2.4 W4: Enter in the title slide's body placeholder ended the session

Diagnosis, confirmed. `startEdit` read `multiline` through `blockById`, which finds top level blocks only, so the title slide's lead (a slide field, not a block) was never multiline and Enter finished the session.

Fix. `isMultilineType(type, pointer)` in `packages/schema/src/catalog.ts` judges a pointer by its block type alone. `startEdit` resolves a pseudo block's type through `blockTypeOf` when `blockById` finds nothing; a title's lead is a paragraph, whose `/text` is multiline, so Enter in the subtitle placeholder makes a line break. The title slide's `lead` field takes `multilineTextSchema` in `packages/schema/src/deck.ts`, a superset of the one line schema, so every existing deck validates with no migration, and `render/slide.ts` draws the lead with `renderMultiline`, which is byte for byte the one line render when the lead holds one paragraph. The heading stays a one line field, so Enter on the title still ends the session.

Tests. `packages/schema/src/catalog.test.ts` (`isMultilineType`) and `packages/schema/src/validate.test.ts` (a paragraph break is accepted in a title lead and refused in its heading). The walk: "Enter in the body makes a line break and the next words land on it" and "Shift Enter in the body makes a line break too".

Files: `packages/schema/src/catalog.ts`, `packages/viewer/src/Editor.tsx`, `packages/schema/src/deck.ts`, `packages/render/src/slide.ts`, `packages/schema/src/catalog.test.ts`, `packages/schema/src/validate.test.ts`.

### 2.5 W10: Cmd Z inside a text session left the text as it was

Diagnosis, pinned this round. The walk records the history and the snackbar for it, and a focused reproduction against the dev server (`scratchpad/hotfix4/dbg-undo.mjs`) showed the mechanism. Cmd Z inside the run calls `finish('undo')` and then `onUndo()` in the same event. `finish` ends the session, which schedules the Editor's re-render; `onUndo` runs `controller.undo()`, which pops the entry and commits its inverse, and the document heading did change (the reproduction logged the title's heading before and after the commit: "Quarterly review undo" then "Quarterly review"). The document changed but the run stayed stale, because the undo's document change was batched with the session end's re-render and lost. A second cause was the undo grouping: `typingKeyOf` recognised a `text.splice` on a block's run but not the `slide.set` a title or statement slide's text burst writes, so each 100 ms burst of a title was its own undo step.

Fix. In `InlineText.tsx` the undo and the redo run on the next task after `finish`, so the document change is a re-render of its own and is not batched away with the session end. `typingKeyOf` (moved to `apps/studio/src/editor/typing-key.ts`) now names the field of a title or statement slide's burst as well as a block's run, so the bursts of one word fold into one undo step. Redo works the same way.

Tests. `apps/studio/src/editor/typing-key.test.ts`: a burst on a block's run and a burst on a title or statement slide's text field both name one Text, and every other write is its own step. The walk: "Cmd Z inside the text undoes the typed word as one step" and "Cmd Shift Z redoes it".

Files: `packages/viewer/src/InlineText.tsx`, `apps/studio/src/editor/typing-key.ts` (new), `apps/studio/src/editor/typing-key.test.ts` (new), `apps/studio/src/editor/controller.tsx` (imports the moved function).

### 2.6 W9: a converted title kept its heading at the width of its text

Diagnosis, confirmed. `.left-mid` on the title slide is absolutely positioned with a left edge and no width, so its heading and lead shrink to their text; the canvas conversion measures that shrink wrapped box and writes it as the object's frame, where Google keeps the placeholder's width, so a longer title wrapped inside a narrow box and split words.

Fix. `.left-mid` takes `right: 0` in `packages/theme/src/gt-ink-paper/sheet.css`, so its text fields span the content box the way a placeholder frame does. A left aligned text draws the same at either width, so the compare to shoot gate is unchanged. The heading the conversion measures is now the column's width, and a longer title wraps at the words.

Tests. `scripts/compare-to-shoot.mjs` at 0.5 percent and `scripts/canvas-fidelity.mjs` stay green. The walk: "the converted short title keeps a wide box and wraps a long title at word boundaries" and "the converted title wraps at word boundaries and stays clear of the body placeholder".

Files: `packages/theme/src/gt-ink-paper/sheet.css`.

### 2.7 W8: the code panel did not fill its box and its marks kept a fixed size

Diagnosis, confirmed. No canvas rule sized a positioned panel, so it kept its content height inside a taller box, and `panel.ts` wrote the two term marks at 25 by 16 and 50 by 32 whatever the box.

Fix. `block-css.ts` gives `.free > .panel` `height: 100%`, so the panel fills its box (its width already follows the box as a block child). `panel.ts` writes the two term marks of a positioned panel with a class and the symbol's `viewBox` and no fixed size, and `block-css.ts` sizes them by the box height (`mark-s` at half, `mark-l` at the whole), so the marks scale with the box on a terminal bench. A flow panel keeps its fixed marks byte for byte.

Tests. `packages/render/src/__tests__/blocks.test.ts`: a flow panel writes the fixed sizes, a panel object writes the classed marks with the symbol's viewBox, and `block-css.ts` carries the fill and mark rules. The walk: the code panel resize rows record the panel filling its box and each mark tracking the box height.

Files: `packages/render/src/blocks/panel.ts`, `packages/render/src/block-css.ts`, `packages/render/src/__tests__/blocks.test.ts`.

### 2.8 The caret keys inside the canvas run

Diagnosis, confirmed against the shipped key tables. The stage's own key table yields every key while a run is being edited, but the shell's key owner (`useEditorKeys`) skipped only the bare keys and the run owned chords inside the canvas run, so Cmd Up and Cmd Down (Move slide up and down, Bring forward and Send backward), PageUp and PageDown (the filmstrip) and their variants still ran their chord and the caret did not move. This is the path by which the orchestrator's Home and End probe and Kevin's keystrokes landed out of order.

Fix. `useEditorKeys.ts` returns early for a caret key pressed inside the canvas run, whatever the modifiers, so Home, End, PageUp, PageDown and the arrows with Shift, Cmd and Option belong to the text and never to a slide or an object. The caret keys are named in `CARET_KEYS` and the rule is `isCaretKeyInCanvasText`.

Tests. `packages/viewer/src/__tests__/editor-keys.test.ts` asserts the stage's key table yields every caret key with every modifier while editing; `packages/chrome/src/__tests__/use-editor-keys.test.tsx` asserts the shell runs and prevents nothing for every caret key with every modifier from the run, and still matches the chord from the page body. The walk: "Cmd Down inside the title moves the caret to the text end and moves no slide or object", "Cmd Up inside the title moves the caret to the text start", and "PageUp, PageDown, Shift End and Cmd Shift Up inside the title change no slide and keep the session".

Files: `packages/chrome/src/useEditorKeys.ts`, `packages/viewer/src/__tests__/editor-keys.test.ts`, `packages/chrome/src/__tests__/use-editor-keys.test.tsx`.

### 2.9 W5: the layout picker did not close on Escape

Diagnosis, confirmed. The layout plate is a dialog whose Escape handler is its own `onKeyDown`, so it answered Escape only while focus was inside it; opened by a click on the toolbar button the focus stays on that button, outside the plate.

Fix. The plate's effect adds a document capture Escape listener that closes it and returns the focus, the way the sidebar and the menus close. The plate's own `onKeyDown` still serves a keyboard user whose focus is inside it, and the outside press still closes it.

Test. The walk: "the layout picker opens from the toolbar and closes with Escape".

Files: `packages/chrome/src/EditorShell.tsx`.

### 2.10 W6 settled: grouping by the keyboard and the menu works

The walk's earlier run could not establish grouping, because the walk's own Cmd G probe (Cmd G is Find next) opened the Find and replace dialog, whose input then took the chords and the clicks that followed, so the two object selection was lost before the group step. `apps/studio/e2e/objects.spec.ts` already proves Cmd Option G groups two objects and writes one `pos/group` per member, so grouping is not a defect. The walk now re-establishes a clean two object selection before the group step, independent of the Cmd G probe, and the group, the group resize and the ungroup rows drive it.

### 2.11 Deferred

- W7, severity 1: a picture object's frame runs about 12 sheet px past its box, because a shot figure keeps its picture's aspect height and an empty caption adds a row and the 12 px grid gap. The correct fix (the shot fills its box and its picture covers it) is not byte neutral for a converted shot: it moved `gt-brand/dossier` 2.7 percent over the 0.5 percent fidelity budget, so it needs a design decision about how a shot fits its box on the canvas rather than the aspect fit it keeps in the flow. Round five lane B4 owns `packages/render` and the canvas (`packages/render/src/block-css.ts`, `packages/render/src/blocks/figures.ts`); MILESTONES-5 "Owns", B4.
- W11, severity 2, intermittent: the toolbar's Undo after a resize does nothing about once in three hundred tries on the blob tier. It did not reproduce on the memory tier here, and the candidate is hotfix 2 cause A5 (an undo write based one revision low after a fast pair of writes, refused as stale). It needs the blob tier to reproduce and belongs to the sync engine. Round five lane B7 (SPEC-5-amendments A6) owns the write queue and the rebase functions the controller imports.

The icon and mark "off" resize rows (the se and sw handles under some modifiers) and the picture "content did not scale" rows are the walk's own, not the product's: the walk drags with the snaps on, so a dragged edge snaps a few pixels off the exact model box, and a shot's aspect fit is the W7 defect above. They are recorded in the table, not counted as product defects.

### 3.2 The mark in a surface rendered without block attributes

Diagnosis, from the kept PDF gate output (`TURBOSLIDE_KEEP_EXPORT_TEST=1`): the PDF page of `canvas-title` draws the mark object at its 132 by 84 box, and the reference the gate compares it with (`pdf/build.ts` `gatePages`: `renderDeck(..., { blockAttrs: false, present: true, chrome: true })` shot at 2x in the same browser) draws the glyph at 236 by 150, centred in a 300 by 150 svg that starts 32 px left of the box and overlaps the heading. The W2 rule of section 2.2, `.ts-sheet .free > svg[data-type="mark"] { width: 100%; height: 100% }`, keys on `data-type`, and `rootAttrs` writes `data-block` and `data-type` only when `ctx.blockAttrs` is true; the present surface, the deck build (`turboslide build`, checked: its two mark svgs read `<svg fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true">`) and a flatten sheet render without them. An svg with neither a size attribute nor a rule that reaches it takes the browser's replaced element default, 300 by 150, and the symbol is fitted inside it. The studio's stage and the canvas-fidelity gate render with block attributes, which is why the fixer's gates held; the icon (hotfix 3) and the diagram key their rules on a class (`svg.icon-block`, `svg.dia`) and were never affected.

The fix, in the fixer's files: `markSvg` with `sized` false adds the class `mark-block` (merged into the block's own class when it has one; a sized flow mark is untouched, byte for byte), and block-css.ts keys the rule on `svg.mark-block` (the `data-type` selector is gone, so no surface depends on the attribute). `blocks.test.ts`: the mark object test asserts the class and the rule, and a new case renders the mark object with `blockAttrs` off and asserts the class is present and no `data-type` is; the eight `canvas.test.ts` snapshots were updated once more (the positioned mark's svg gains `class="mark-block"`; nothing else in them changed but the W9 widths of 3.3). `gslides-fixture.test.ts` afterwards: 15 passed, the PDF gate's 28 pages under the fail line.

### 3.4 The walk's aspect locked corners

The seven "off" resize rows of the fixer's run (the icon's se and sw handles plain and with Alt, the icon's se at zoom 200, the mark's se and sw with Alt) were the walk's expectation, not the product's geometry: `schema/canvas.ts` `ASPECT_LOCKED_KINDS` keeps the aspect ratio from a corner handle without Shift for the picture, the icon, the material, the mark and the plate (R04 B7, as Google's image handles do), the axis with the larger relative change leads and the other follows, and a snapped leading edge moves the following axis by the ratio (the icon's 240 by 150 dragged 60 by 40 from se lands at 312 by 195 when the bottom edge snaps to 570, the ratio 1.6 kept). `expectedPos` computed the free box. The walk now judges a corner drag on an aspect locked kind the way it judges Shift, by the kept ratio and the growth in the dragged direction, plus the product's anchor: a plain corner keeps the opposite corner within the 10 px tolerance and Alt keeps the centre. A shot resizes freely and keeps the free expectation.

### 3.7 The redo after an undo inside the text on the blob tier

The first ship attempt's walk on the preview `turboslide-r92q2dbtf` failed at its row 22, "Cmd Shift Z redoes it": the text stayed at the undone form. Its row 21 recorded the mechanism beside the passing undo: the snackbar read "Revision r12 arrived from outside this editor and is shown. Reload" with no author, `sync` read revision 12 then 13, and the redo stack was empty afterwards. The harness ended that attempt while it was reproducing the failure; this attempt read the code path instead and then reproduced the pair on the preview.

Diagnosis. Cmd Z inside the run calls `finish('undo')`, whose write is the burst's `slide.set`, and the undo runs on the next task (section 2.5), so its write follows the burst's write at once: the room client posts one batch at a time, so the undo's POST leaves when the burst's answer arrives. On the blob tier `admitOnBlob` bases the write on `room.live()`, which reads the instance's mirror of the deck (`packages/store/src/blob-store.ts` `syncNow`), and that mirror is re-read from the store only when its last sync is older than `syncTtlMs`, 750 ms. Under fluid compute the two POSTs can land on two instances: the second instance's mirror, synced by an earlier burst inside the window, still carries revision 11 while the first instance committed the burst as revision 12, so the channel appends with base 11, the store's `ifMatch` refuses the base and the append answers `{ ok: false, head: 12 }`, which the ops route returns as a 409 `resync`. The room client reloads the document at revision 12 and re-sends the undo write, which lands as revision 13. The reload calls the controller's `onResync`, which cleared the history and its transform clocks unconditionally and showed the external revision banner for the reloaded revision. The undo's history entry had been moved to the redo stack by `history.undo()` before its write, so the clear emptied the redo stack: Cmd Shift Z found nothing to redo. The banner named the tab's own write as one that arrived from outside. The same clear is the likely path of the deferred W11 (the toolbar's Undo after a resize doing nothing about once in three hundred tries): an undo whose entry was cleared by a resync in the same window.

The clear is right when a resync brings entries the tab never applied: `transformSince` moves an inverse past the remote entries in the room client's recent log, and entries a reload brought in wholesale are not in it. It is wrong when the reload lands at or below the revision the tab has acknowledged: every revision up to the head is already applied, the recent log and the clocks are valid, and the refused write is re-sent after the reload.

Fix. `apps/studio/src/editor/resync-history.ts` (new) carries the rule, `resyncBroughtUnseen(fresh, known)`: true when the reloaded document's revision is above the last revision this tab acknowledged (the controller's `serverRevision`, which follows the room client's acknowledged revision through `onStatus` and `onChange`). `controller.tsx` `onResync` clears the history and the clocks and shows the external banner only then; a reload at or below the known revision keeps the history and shows no banner. The versions, the leases and the server revision follow the reload as before.

Test. `apps/studio/src/editor/resync-history.test.ts`: the reload at the acknowledged revision (the walk's row 21: the burst at r12, the undo refused, the reload at r12) keeps the history; a reload behind it (a stream reset) keeps it; a reload above it clears it; a fresh deck's first reload at revision 0 keeps it and one at revision 1 clears it. `cd apps/studio && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/editor`: 12 passed (3 files). The walk: rows 21 and 22 on the preview and on production, in section 3.6 and 3.8.

The reproduction. `scratchpad/ship4/redo-probe.mjs` (the first attempt's script) types a word in a fresh deck's title, Cmd Z inside the session, then Cmd Shift Z, and trashes the deck; six tries against the first attempt's preview `r92q2dbtf` (before this fix) all passed, with revisions 1 or 2 through 4 and no reject, so the refused base needs a second instance whose mirror is warm inside the window, which a fresh deck with two writes rarely meets and the walk's title, written by eleven bursts before the undo, met on the first attempt. The path is intermittent by routing; the fix removes its effect on the history whichever instance admits the write. The stale mirror at admission itself (an admission that reads a mirror inside the sync window rather than the store's head) stays with round five lane B7 beside W11, the sync engine's lane; it costs one extra round trip and no data.

Files: `apps/studio/src/editor/resync-history.ts` (new), `apps/studio/src/editor/resync-history.test.ts` (new), `apps/studio/src/editor/controller.tsx`.
